messages:
maria gonzalez: quick thread — proposing a new default canary profile for model version upgrades. want feedback on percent steps, timing, and what we expose in the console vs API. :eyes:

samir patel: do you have a concrete example of the step schedule? easier to iterate on exact numbers than vague 'gradual'.

maria gonzalez: yup. my recommendation: small micro-steps early, then exponential-ish growth. something like:
```json
{
  "steps": [
    {"percent": 0.1, "duration_min": 30},
    {"percent": 0.5, "duration_min": 30},
    {"percent": 1, "duration_min": 60},
    {"percent": 5, "duration_min": 120},
    {"percent": 10, "duration_min": 240},
    {"percent": 25, "duration_min": 360},
    {"percent": 50, "duration_min": 720},
    {"percent": 100, "duration_min": 0}
  ]
}
```
this favors catching regressions early while not taking forever for small-scale infra-limited customers.

liam cho: i like the micro-steps. question: duration_min semantics — wall time vs observed-stable window? e.g., do we require N minutes after metric stablization or just wait X wall minutes and then evaluate?

maria gonzalez: prefer a hybrid: minimum wall time per step (to collect traffic), plus an optional "evaluation window" setting that can pause progression until telemetry criteria are met. default evaluation_window = 0 (meaning no pause).

anya ivanova: UX/console note: if we expose both steps and evaluation windows, the UI needs to make it super obvious which is gating. users confuse ramp duration with health-gate duration all the time. recommend we show a simple inline summary: "Auto-advance: ON/OFF" and a compact timeline view.

krishna rao: telemetry gating — we need an agreed set of guard metrics and thresholds. my proposal: request_error_rate (5xx + 4xx-expected) delta > 2x baseline, p95 latency increase > 30% and conversation-quality regression (if available) flagged by evals. any one trigger -> pause and roll back option surfaced.

zach tanner: +1 on those metrics. also add token-cost-per-request delta > 20% as a soft signal. sometimes quantization/model changes blow cost slightly and we should surface that.

samir patel: API shape discussion: should the rollout config be a single blob (like maria's JSON) or composable objects (steps + gates + fallback policy) with references? Composable allows reuse across models.

maria gonzalez: prefer composable. example: reference a "step_profile_id" and "gate_profile_id". that way console shows profile catalog and engs can change profiles without editing every model rollout.

deploy-bot: CI check: rollout schema v2 detected. validating object shape... PASSED. (build #4821) :white_check_mark:

liam cho: what about drift/traffic spikes — if traffic suddenly jumps at 5% because of organic routing, the absolute # of requests could cause noisy metrics. maybe we should normalize by request count and require a minimum sample size before evaluating gates.

krishna rao: yes, minimum_sample_size required. default 500 requests per step before evaluating. if not enough samples, auto-extend duration up to 4x before marking inconclusive.

anya ivanova: Console UX: add a little tooltip "min samples" and show a running counter. users get anxiety when steps stall — show reasons (waiting for samples, paused by gate, manual hold).

zach tanner: rollback semantics: immediate rollback vs staged rollback? i'd lean staged: when a gate trips, reduce to previous healthy step (not full 0) and pause. immediate full rollback should be an explicit option. default behavior: step-back-to previous and pause for manual review.

maria gonzalez: agree. default: back one step and pause. expose a flag in API to force full rollback. also store the snapshot of traffic slices for auditing.

samir patel: A/B testing integration: we need experiment IDs and variant labels in the rollout metadata so metrics tie into our experiments pipeline. also IMHO treat A/B as a separate "experimented rollout" type where control is explicitly referenced.

krishna rao: yes — require optional fields: experiment_id, variant_id. telemetry will attach those tags.

liam cho: one more edge: overlapping rollouts. what if there are two model upgrades targeting different routes but same model family and shared infra? routing layer needs to prioritize capacity and maybe apply backpressure. should we add a per-customer concurrency quota to the rollout config so the scheduler can respect it?

maria gonzalez: add optional quota_hint: {max_qps, max_concurrency}. scheduler can use it to avoid oversubscribing nodes. fallback path remains to route to previous version when over quota.

anya ivanova: UI: when user launches rollout, present a pre-flight summary with top guard metrics, quota hints, experiment tags, and a single-click confirm. also display an estimated time-to-complete based on recent traffic.

zach tanner: tiny implementation nit: when serializing to database, store step list normalized as integer percents (not floats) to avoid precision shenanigans. e.g., 0.1% -> 0.1 allowed but store as milli-percent if needed.

maria gonzalez: noted. will update proto.

samir patel: next steps: maria to update API proto with composable profiles, krishna to draft gate thresholds doc, anya to prototype console summary UI, liam/zach to review scheduler quota integration. i'll take API review once proto is in.

maria gonzalez: thanks all. i'll push a PR with schema + example and tag reviewers. planning to land default profile v2 next week. :thumbsup:
